concept.name: Stop run
concept.definition: A move that pushes price through a level where stop-loss orders are known or presumed to cluster, triggering them, often followed by a quick reversal. In SMC vocabulary this is the liquidity sweep; in classical terms it overlaps with the false breakout. The deliberate-targeting framing is an inference, not an observable fact.
concept.intuition: Obvious levels have crowds of stops parked behind them; a push through sets off that cascade in one quick burst.
concept.mechanics: Identified by the footprint: a fast trade through a well-watched swing high/low or round number, a burst of activity as stops execute, and (in the sweep reading) failure to hold beyond the level. Buy stops sit above highs, sell stops below lows, so the run direction names the pool being executed.
concept.failure_modes: Not every run through a level reverses — sometimes the stop cascade fuels a genuine breakout; distinguishing the two requires waiting for the close and follow-through.
concept.misconceptions: That brokers or market makers visibly hunt individual retail stops; academic work documents stop clustering and unusual behavior at such levels, but the personalized stop-hunt story is contested.
concept.example: A pair trades two ticks below an obvious equal-lows level, triggering clustered sell stops, then closes back above the level within the same bar — a classic stop-run footprint.
